data.name: Ramavath
data.long_meaning: The name Ramavath is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Rama', which means 'Joy'. In Hinduism, Rama is the seventh avatar of Lord Vishnu and the prince of Ayodhya. He is known for his unwavering devotion to his wife Sita and his commitment to dharma.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Ramavath signifies the divine presence of Lord Rama within an individual, embodying the qualities of strength, courage, and devotion. It is believed that those named Ramavath will be blessed with victory over adversity and the inner strength to overcome challenges.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ramavath has deep cultural significance in Hinduism, especially in India. Rama is considered one of the most revered and celebrated deities in Hinduism. His story is portrayed in various Hindu texts including the Ramayana, an epic poem written by Sage Valmiki. Rama is also the central figure in various forms of art, literature, and folklore. Numerous temples dedicated to Lord Rama can be found throughout India, and during the festival of Diwali (Deepavali), Rama's victorious return to Ayodhya is commemorated with great joy and celebration.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ramavath holds spiritual significance as it is derived from the name of Lord Rama, who embodies virtues such as truthfulness, righteousness, compassion, and courage. For Hindus, the name Ramavath serves as a reminder of the importance of leading a life centered on dharma, artha, kama, and moksha (duty, wealth, desire, and liberation). It represents the pursuit of joy, peace, and blessings from the divine. The name also incorporates the qualities of Rama, such as unwavering devotion to one's wife and commitment to dharma, which folks carrying the name aim to uphold in their lives.
